issues.description: Deprecation message omits the redirect_stderr equivalence for a parameter-only call
issues.detail: The warning text bundles both stdlib functions into one message, but a caller using only redirected(stdout=...) is told to use two things. Minor, but the message complects the two redirections that contextlib keeps as separate, simple values. A one-line note that they are independent context managers would match the actual decomposition.

issues.description: Deprecation docstring has a typo (stlib) in user-facing rendered docs
issues.detail: The .. deprecated:: 4.3 block reads "Use the stlib's" instead of "stdlib's". This renders into Sphinx output and the news fragment cross-references. Small, but the value here is documentation — get the spelling right since this is the artifact users actually read when they hit the warning.

review.summary: SIMPLE. This change is the right direction: it removes a piece of incidental complexity (a bespoke context manager that was complecting two independent stdout/stderr redirections into one signature) in favor of two separate, composable stdlib primitives that already model the concern as values pushed to the edges. The deprecation path is conservative and well-staged — warning now, removal in 5.0, internal tests already migrated as the proof. The remaining nits are cosmetic: a typo in the rendered deprecation directive and a slightly muddled warning message. The question that should have been asked first — "is this a library or a framework problem?" — was asked, and the answer (library, and the stdlib already has it) was honored. Ship.
